text: This is for every man that needs Lindsay Clancy to be held accountable for what she did. Men are overwhelmingly responsible for all murders and rapes. Not some, not the majority, but almost all of them. If you need Lindsay Clancy to be held accountable that bad, then you need men to be held accountable way more, because that justice bone needs to be exercised, right? Right. That's literally the point. Everyone should be held accountable for what they do, men or women. And yes, the majority of violent crime is committed by men, that is true. But 90% of violent offenders being men does not mean 90% of men are violent offenders. Those are two completely different statistics. It means that among the very small group of people committing violent crimes, most are male. The available data strongly suggests that in any given year, significantly less than 1% of men commit violent crimes. More than 99% of men are not doing that. So you are taking the actions of a tiny fraction of men and somehow using them to tell the rest of men that they don't get to talk about accountability? How does that make any sense? The overwhelming majority of men have absolutely no problem holding violent men accountable. Murderers? Put them in prison. Rapists? Put them in prison. Men who hurt children? Absolutely put them in prison. That's the whole point. And actually, even the prison culture itself makes this even more obvious. There's a documented informal hierarchy in men's prisons, where people who commit certain crimes against children are at the very bottom. Those guys can be specifically targeted by other prisoners. Think about what that means. Even men who are themselves in prison, including violent criminals, can look at somebody who victimizes children and think, you're an absolute scum. So when people online say, if a man strangles his three little children, you wouldn't see hundreds of men outside the courthouse supporting him, I think they have a point. And if hundreds of men did show up outside that courthouse, I have a feeling they would be there for a very different reason. Now, to be completely clear, I still support Lindsay Clancy getting a fair trial. The jury should hear all the evidence and decide whether she was criminally responsible when she killed her children. If she knew what she was doing and was criminally responsible, then, in my opinion, she should spend the rest of her life in prison. If she genuinely was psychotic to the point that she was legally not responsible, then I think she should spend the rest of her life in a secure psychiatric hospital. And yes, I think it is shameful that under Massachusetts law, that second outcome does not necessarily have to be permanent. Because if she is found not criminally responsible, she can be sent to psychiatric hospital, but she does not automatically stay there for life. Her condition can be reviewed. And if at some point doctors and the court decide that she's no longer mentally ill and dangerous enough to keep confined, she can be released. She can go free and go back to living her life. Hell yeah, I have a serious problem with that. She strangled her three defenseless little children. I do not think the eventual outcome for her should ever be, you are better now, so you get to be completely free again. Because Cora, Dawson, and Callan don't get their lives back. So no, saying men commit most violent crimes does not mean most men commit violent crimes. And it especially does not mean men lose the right to demand accountability when a woman kills three children. Holding male criminals accountable and holding Lindsay Clancy accountable are not contradictory positions. They are the exact same position.
